newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares rally at noon before holiday.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares rally at noon before holiday.

text.p: Shenzhen's B shares staged a rebound at midday on Friday ahead of the Hong Kong handover holiday, supported by institutional buying in shares of firms expected to post robust 1997 interim results, brokers said.
The B share index rallied 0.28 points or 0.20 percent to 144.09 after losses for four straight trade days. Turnover was HK$47 million.
The domestic A share market dipped 0.75 points or 0.16 percent to 459.34, with investors seen pulling out before the long holiday, brokers said.
The Shenzhen Stock Exchange has announced it will close on June 30 and July 1 to mark the handover and trading will resume on Wednesday, July 2.
"The B share market seems to have bottomed out above the 140-point level, which should be a strong medium-term support," a B share analyst at China Guotai Securities said.

Analysts said that active selective buying in firms likely to report strong 1997 first-half results in the forthcoming interim reporting season could boost sentiment in both the A and B share markets in July.
They said they expected most listed firms to report slightly better first-half results this year with the effect of last year's two interest rate cuts flowing through to the 1997 interim reports.
"People have begun shifting attention to counters aided by talk of strong interim earnings," an analyst at Central-South Securities said.
But worries that Beijing may carry out new counter-speculation measures in July will cap share rises, the analysts said.
In the B share market, conglomerate Shenzhen Zhonghao was the best performer with a rise of HK$0.18 or 5.81 percent to HK$3.28. But volume was a paper-thin 100 shares.

Chenming Paper, helped by investor optimism over its interim profits, jumped HK$0.36 or 5.08 percent to HK$7.45 to be the third sharpest gainer, brokers said. It was the most actively traded issue on volume of 2.0 million shares.
Jiujiang Chemical Fibre was the weakest performer in the A share maket, slumping 0.54 yuan or 5.69 percent to 8.95 yuan.
